tasks.task: Write show notes, titles and chapters from a transcript

items.when: Before writing, to cut a long transcript down to the few parts worth quoting
When the episode is recorded and you need titles, summary, takeaways, timestamps and chapters
When you only have rough notes, not a full transcript, and still need notes with links
When the episode also goes on YouTube and the chapter list must follow its rules
When the three titles feel alike, to see several different angles
When you have a title list, to score each read alone and keep the best three
When the notes repeat a guest's facts or numbers, to check each before publishing

tasks.task: Plan an episode and its timed run sheet

items.when: When a guest or topic is chosen, to run every step from booking to release in order
When the topic is broad, to find the one case the episode should be built on
Before recording, to set the promise, the segments, the questions and the timings
When it is a first episode, to get a pilot hook, a timed run sheet and a recording plan
When the outline is a list of topics, to find what happened and what it meant
Before writing questions, to see the topic from the guest's side: what they want and why
When you need open questions with follow-ups in an order that builds
When the questions invite rehearsed answers, to find the one that gets a real story
When you need a scored shortlist, the booking steps and a signed release
When you want one named guest, and again when they say yes and need a prep pack
When the pitch and the follow-ups must sound like the host and name something specific
When the guest has never heard of the show, to try a first message read in seconds
Before sending the pitch, to cut it and check it has one clear ask

tasks.task: Log rights and consent before release

items.when: Before release, or when asked whether a song, clip or voice can be used
When a guest appears, to confirm consent on tape and a signed release are on file
When a giveaway, promotion or sponsor message must follow the law where listeners are

tasks.task: Pick clips and write the promo kit

items.when: When you have the transcript, to find the best five moments to clip
When the episode is final and you need three clips, the posts and the email
When one strong passage should become a post that stands alone
When the episode email needs a subject line, to compare several angles
When clips are chosen, to score each opening and rewrite the weak ones
When the client wants captioned short clips cut from the recording for review
When the promo kit is finished, so a fresh reader checks it against the brief as the host would

tasks.task: Caption clips and prepare the video version

items.when: When clips need timed captions in the show's font and a subtitle file
When clips and captions are cut by editing the transcript
When the episode goes on YouTube and needs a title, description, tags and timestamps
Before upload, to check titles for length and repeats beside the thumbnail idea

tasks.task: Make and clean a transcript with speaker labels

items.when: When you have the audio and need the words written out with each speaker labelled
When you also need word timings and a subtitle file
When the transcript will be published, to make it readable and accessible
Before it goes on the episode page, to fix names, terms and slips

tasks.task: Plan the edit of a raw recording

items.when: When you have the raw file and need clean speech, a timed cut list and chapters
When the talk runs long, to decide in passes what stays
When the recording has background noise or music under the speech
When voice, music and effects need a timed plan before the final mix
When the edit is clean but flat, to listen for the part worth building around

tasks.task: Check an episode before it goes live

items.when: Before publishing, to check file format, loudness, feed basics and the episode page
When you have the file, to measure loudness, noise and speech quality
When the check finds noise that must be fixed before release

tasks.task: Plan a season of episodes and guests

items.when: Before listing episodes, to find the few subjects the host can truly own
Before a new season, to get episodes, guests to pitch and a rhythm the host can keep
When the season plan must also cover positioning and growth on each platform
When a client wants to start a podcast or restart one that stopped
When the show needs its positioning and a first-season plan for the main platforms
When the idea needs testing as one pilot before a full season
When the show has no name yet, to compare five name ideas and why each fits listeners
When there is a launch date, to plan the teaser, the preview and launch day
Before the launch plan is set, to compare two plans that spend the time and budget differently

tasks.task: Write a sponsor read with disclosure

items.when: When an episode carries a sponsor and the host reads the message
When the read needs a way in, to get ten openings the host could say naturally
Before recording, to fix lines that trip when spoken
Before the sponsor signs off, to sort each claim as fine, needs proof or cut
Before the read is recorded, to confirm the sponsor's link, code and offer work for a listener today
When another show or brand shares the audience, to plan a joint push and the pitch
When the show needs sponsor tiers and pitch copy; built for events, so adapt the benefits
When the pitch to a sponsor or partner must sound like the host

tasks.task: Review the show's month and decide what to change

items.when: After the last release of the month, to read the numbers and pick what to change
When you have the host's export and need trends in plain words
When the report leans on totals, to swap them for numbers that show real listening
When the month's best episodes should be turned into more content

tasks.task: Turn an episode into an article or newsletter

items.when: When the transcript should become a tidy article with a title, summary and headings
When one episode should feed a series of emails, posts and clips
When the article needs its own title, to compare several angles
When the article is drafted, to fix lines that read as machine written
Before the article is handed over, so a fresh reader says what a new listener could not follow

tasks.task: Script the intro and outro and brief the music bed

items.when: When the intro is voiced, to write it with pacing and pauses marked
When the show needs a theme or a bed described by genre, tempo and instruments
When the host wants to hear two or three rough themes before choosing
When the intro is drafted, to fix lines that trip when spoken

tasks.task: Write a trailer or solo episode script

items.when: When one voice carries the piece and it must be shaped for the ear
When the script needs clear speakers, pacing and a set length
When the trailer's first ten seconds are weak, to compare openings
When a solo episode explains something, to start from one ordinary thing and ask why
Before recording, to catch every line that reads well but speaks badly
When the script is final, so a fresh reviewer checks it against the brief before anyone records

tasks.task: Release an episode in another language

items.when: When the episode should exist in other languages and keep each speaker's voice
When the show notes and titles need a natural version in the new language

always.when: When notes, posts or reads state facts or numbers, to check each one
Before delivery, to catch stock phrases that make copy read as machine written
Last step before publishing, to catch slips and wrong names

helpers.when: When the episode needs a full video edit, not only clips and captions
When the promo kit needs scheduling, replies and a channel plan
When the show is ready for a rate card, a sponsor deck and sponsor prospecting
When the show needs cover art, episode cards or quote cards designed
When a sponsor wants a produced ad, a jingle or a sonic logo
When the video version should grow as a channel in its own right
